title: Reliability Collab Scrumburst — 45-Day Cross-Functional SLO Playbook
summary: A compact 45-day experiment to fast-track SLO definition, observability, and operational playbooks for a small set of model-serving endpoints. The goal is to prove a repeatable, cross-functional cadence (the 'scrumburst') that pairs SRE, serving-runtime, product, and observability to deliver measurable reliability improvements with minimal overhead.
objectives: Define clear, consumer-oriented SLOs for 3 pilot services (text-gen-api, embedder, reranker)
Ship end-to-end monitoring + alert rules with ownership and playbook links
Implement and test one automated fallback policy per service (model-variant or region fallback)
Run a single-week canary/rollback drill and capture lessons for org-wide SLO onboarding
stakeholders: SRE: Maya Chen (program lead), Ravi Patel (oncall lead)
Serving Runtime: Jun Park (engineer), Lena Ortiz (perf lead)
timeline: Day 0-7 Discovery: map SLAs, consumer journeys, and current signals. Day 8-14 Design: draft SLOs, alert thresholds, and acceptable error budgets. Day 15-30 Build: implement metrics, dashboards, and fallback automation; integrate into alerting. Day 31-38 Shakeout: run internal drills, fix gaps. Day 39-45 Canary & Retrospective: run the canary, execute rollback drills, capture artifacts and a playbook template.
milestones: M1 (D7): Consumer-journey heatmap + baseline signal inventory completed
M2 (D14): SLO spec for 3 pilots reviewed and accepted by stakeholders
M3 (D25): Metrics plumbing and dashboards live in observability
M4 (D32): Automated fallback policy implemented and unit-tested
M5 (D45): Canary executed; retrospective + final playbook published
success_metrics: Defined SLOs with owner and a documented measurement window for each pilot
Alert noise reduced: >30% fewer non-actionable page opens during beta week
Canary rollbacks succeed within target MTTR (target: 15 minutes from detection to mitigation)
Playbook reuse: at least 2 additional teams adopt the template within 60 days
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: Instrumentation gaps for tail-latency. Mitigation: start with 95/99/999 p95/p99/p999 and add tracing hotspots; prioritize one critical path first.
Risk: Alert fatigue if naive thresholds are chosen. Mitigation: use aggregated signals + multi-step alert (warning -> action) and require runbook linkage for paging alerts.
Risk: Cross-team scheduling conflicts slow progress. Mitigation: reserve bi-weekly 60-minute syncs and 'office hours' calendar blocks for rapid pairing.
Risk: Fallback automation causes inconsistent UX. Mitigation: simulate fallback in staging and include consumer-impact note in release checklist.
Risk: Customer-facing SLA mismatches. Mitigation: involve Solutions/CS in SLO acceptance criteria and label SLOs as internal vs contractual.
runbook_snippets: Incident triage (short form): 1) Detect: alert fires with link to dashboard + last 15m traces. 2) Classify: latency vs error vs throughput; check region/fleet impact. 3) Immediate mitigation: if error spike, trigger model-variant fallback (playbook link) and reduce traffic via traffic-splitting command. 4) Stabilize: scale up reserved capacity or shift to dedicated pool if autoscaling not enough. 5) Resolve: collect artifact (trace id, API key, sample payloads), close incident with postmortem owner assigned. Automated fallback checklist: verify health probe endpoints, confirm KV-cache warmup time, validate model-compatibility matrix, and ensure telemetry tags are emitted.
